deviations.description: Verification bullet 'Oversized payload (>131,072 bytes) via --argjson with --dry-run exits 0 instead of 126'
deviations.reason: Empirically confirmed (and independently corroborated by the research report at reports/01_fix-argv-ceiling.md line 124) that Linux's MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131,072 bytes) applies to the OS-level execve() that launches state-write.sh's OWN bash-interpreted process, not only to state-write.sh's internal jq invocation. A caller cannot pass a >131,072-byte raw value via literal `--argjson NAME VALUE` on state-write.sh's own command line at all -- the shell fails to exec state-write.sh itself (exit 126) before any internal script code (including this phase's spill logic) ever runs. This means the internal --argjson spill path can only ever be exercised for values in roughly (100000, ~131072] bytes (where state-write.sh's own invocation still succeeds) -- and in that narrow range jq itself would have accepted the value directly anyway, since jq's own MAX_ARG_STRLEN ceiling is the same constant. The spill path is therefore verified working end-to-end (tested at 128,890 bytes) but is not reachable for genuinely oversized (>131,072-byte) payloads. Genuinely unbounded payloads are handled by the OTHER half of this phase's deliverable: `--argjson-file NAME PATH`, which was tested successfully with a 223,891-byte file (PATH is a short argv token, so it never hits the ceiling, no matter how large the file's contents are).
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- verification demonstrated via --argjson-file for genuinely oversized payloads and via an in-range 128,890-byte --argjson case for the spill path itself, since a >131,072-byte value cannot reach state-write.sh's own $3 at all; see progress file for full analysis)*

deviations.description: Non-Goals: 'No changes to skill-todo/SKILL.md or commands/todo.md... makes every existing --argjson call site work unchanged'
deviations.type: flagged, not corrected (out of implementer scope)
deviations.reason: Per the deviation above, the one KNOWN real caller hitting this ceiling in production (skill-todo/SKILL.md Stage 10 / commands/todo.md's archival-batch --argjson tasks call, recorded at 168,180 bytes) is NOT actually fixed by transparent spill alone, because 168,180 > 131,072 and the call would still crash at state-write.sh's own invocation before any spill code runs. Achieving a working single-call fix for that specific caller requires migrating it to --argjson-file (writing the payload to a file first, then passing a short PATH argv token) -- a call-site change the plan's Non-Goals section explicitly excludes. This is a plan-level finding, not something this implementation phase can silently correct (revising the plan's scope is the planner's responsibility, not this agent's) -- flagged here and in the implementation summary/handoff for follow-up.
